notice: DEMONSTRATION DATA for the platform redesign's design preview. Every designer and project below is fictional sample content created to review layouts. None of it is real work, a real person or a real published project. Never present it as genuine. Cover artwork is generated by src/build/showcase-art.js from bpozz palettes.

designers.name: Mira S.
designers.headline: Brand identity designer
designers.bio: Mira builds identity systems for independent food and hospitality brands. Her work starts with a single mark and grows into colour, type and packaging rules that a small team can keep consistent on their own.

designers.name: Tomás E.
designers.headline: Illustrator and poster designer
designers.bio: Tomás draws loud posters for festivals and quiet picture books for children. He works in flat shapes and limited palettes so every piece survives screen printing as well as it does on screen.

designers.name: Aiko N.
designers.headline: Type designer
designers.bio: Aiko draws typefaces for interfaces and identities, from compact grotesques to rounded display faces. Each family ships with a specimen that shows how it holds up at the sizes people actually use.

designers.name: Kofi A.
designers.headline: Product designer
designers.bio: Kofi designs calm, practical apps for money, health and everyday planning. He prototypes early, tests with real people and documents every component so engineers can build it once.

designers.name: Sana R.
designers.headline: Editorial designer
designers.bio: Sana lays out magazines, reports and books, and occasionally revives an old typeface along the way. She cares about rhythm across a spread and about type that is still comfortable on page 140.

designers.name: Jonas B.
designers.headline: Packaging designer
designers.bio: Jonas designs packaging and identities for small producers: cider, tea, sauces and the occasional mountain lodge. He prints every label at full size before he trusts it.

designers.name: Elif K.
designers.headline: Illustrator
designers.bio: Elif paints cities, weather and the sea in layered digital gouache. Her campaign work for environmental groups favours a few strong colours over detail.

designers.name: Noah P.
designers.headline: UI designer
designers.bio: Noah designs interfaces for fitness, music and transport products, and the occasional wayfinding system. He likes dark themes, big numbers and motion that explains where things went.

projects.title: Tidewater Coffee Roasters identity
projects.summary: A harbour-side roastery's mark, colour system and café stationery.
body: The roastery sits on an old fishing quay, so the mark borrows the half-circle of a tide gauge and the copper of the boats' fittings. The two halves of the mark change colour by roast, which keeps the whole range recognisable on a busy shelf.
The system covers cups, bags, the café menu board and a stamp for kraft paper, all built from one set of four colours and one typeface.

projects.title: Night Market festival posters
projects.summary: A neon poster series for a three-night street food festival.
body: Each night of the festival gets its own poster, sharing one grid and one oversized headline. Neon pink and cyan stay readable from across the street after dark.
The series was printed as three-colour screen prints, so every shape is a flat colour with no gradients.

projects.title: Kumo Grotesk specimen
projects.summary: A compact grotesque for interfaces, with a specimen in four weights.
body: Kumo is drawn for small sizes first: open apertures, a tall x-height and generous spacing keep it legible in dense interfaces.
The specimen walks from the display weights down to 12px text, with every glyph shown on a grid.

projects.title: Ledger budgeting app
projects.summary: A calm budgeting app that shows one number at a time.
body: Interviews showed that people avoided their budgeting apps because the first screen was a wall of charts. Ledger opens on one number, what is left to spend this week, and keeps the detail one tap away.
The dark and light themes share one token set, documented as a component library for the engineering team.

projects.title: Field Notes quarterly, issue 08
projects.summary: Layout and art direction for a nature writing quarterly.
body: Issue 08 is about autumn harvests, so the palette moves from cream to pumpkin to rust across the issue. Long essays sit on a two-column grid; field reports switch to three.
Every opening spread pairs one large image with a headline set in a single weight, so the pacing comes from scale rather than ornament.

projects.title: Orchard cider packaging
projects.summary: Cans, labels and gift boxes for a small-batch cider maker.
body: Three ciders, three colours: blossom pink, cherry red and orchard green, each on the same can layout so the range reads as one family.
The gift box folds from a single sheet with no glue, shown here as a dieline.

projects.title: Monsoon city illustrations
projects.summary: A series of rainy-season cityscapes in layered teal.
body: The series follows one district through a day of rain, from grey morning to a clear evening over the water.
Every scene is built from three or four layered shapes, so the pieces work as large prints and as small spot illustrations.

projects.title: Pulse fitness dashboard
projects.summary: A training dashboard for coaches and the athletes they follow.
body: Coaches wanted to see a whole squad's week at a glance. The dashboard leads with three numbers per athlete and hides everything else behind one click.
Sunset orange marks effort; green marks recovery. Nothing else on the screen uses colour.

projects.title: Atlas Botanica brand system
projects.summary: An identity for a botanical garden's shop and café.
body: The mark is a seed cut in half, set in the four greens of the garden's glasshouses.
The system was handed over as a short rules sheet the shop staff use for signage and price tags.

projects.title: Saltwater display face
projects.summary: A high-contrast display serif drawn for headlines and posters.
body: Saltwater pushes contrast hard at large sizes and is never meant for text. The glyph grid shows its sharp, ink-trapped joins.
The specimen is set in poppy red on navy, the colours of the harbour flags that inspired it.

projects.title: Folk tales picture book
projects.summary: Spreads for a children's collection of retold folk tales.
body: Each tale opens on a landscape spread in lemon, tangerine and leaf green, with the characters small against big skies.
The flat shapes were planned so the book could be printed in four spot colours.

projects.title: Steep small batch tea tins
projects.summary: A range of tea tins that stack into one long label.
body: The tins share one wrap-around label, so a full shelf reads as a single landscape of jade and mint.
Brewing times sit on the lid, where people actually look while the kettle boils.

projects.title: Line 4 transit wayfinding
projects.summary: A concept wayfinding system for a new light rail line.
body: Amber marks the line on every sign, map and platform edge; navy carries the station names.
This is a self-initiated concept study, not a commissioned system.

projects.title: Museum annual report
projects.summary: A quiet, typographic annual report for a design museum.
body: The report uses one family in two weights, a strict six-column grid and stone-coloured paper.
Figures sit in the margins beside the text that explains them, instead of in a separate section at the back.

projects.title: Streak habit tracker
projects.summary: A habit tracker that celebrates progress without guilt.
body: Missing a day never resets anything to zero; the app shows the longer trend instead.
The flow from sign-up to first habit takes three screens.

projects.title: Desert bloom poster series
projects.summary: Posters for a spring flower festival in burnt orange and honey.
body: Three posters, one for each weekend of the festival, all built on the same large sun.
The type is cropped deliberately on the detail print so the colour carries the piece.

projects.title: Northfold bakery identity
projects.summary: A warm identity for a neighbourhood bakery.
body: Honey and toffee browns, a folded-dough mark and hand-stamped bags.
The colour sheet doubles as the bakery's paint guide for its shopfront.

projects.title: Grain serif revival
projects.summary: A study reviving a 1920s book serif for long reading.
body: Grain started from scans of an old cookbook. The revival keeps its warm, slightly heavy text weight and adds the figures and punctuation a modern book needs.
This is a personal study and is not a released font.

projects.title: Waveform music player
projects.summary: A dark music player with big, glanceable controls.
body: Acid lime marks the one thing you can do next; everything else stays purple and quiet.
The component sheet covers every control state, including loading and offline.

projects.title: Ember hot sauce label range
projects.summary: Labels for a hot sauce range, coded by heat.
body: Heat goes from amber to magenta to neon red, so the hottest bottle is the loudest on the shelf.
The flat label shows the full artwork before it wraps the bottle.

projects.title: Island birds field guide
projects.summary: A pocket field guide with illustrated spreads.
body: Each bird gets one spread: an illustration on the left, a description on the right.
The guide is sized to fit a coat pocket, so the type was tested at its printed size.

projects.title: Care clinic booking flow
projects.summary: A booking flow for a community clinic, tested with older patients.
body: Booking takes three steps, each on its own screen, with large targets and plain language.
The dashboard view lets reception staff see the day's appointments at once.

projects.title: Studio Kiln ceramics identity
projects.summary: A clay-toned identity with a custom logotype.
body: The logotype is drawn, not typed: its round letters echo thrown pots.
Clay red and sage come straight from the studio's glazes.

projects.title: Tide ocean cleanup campaign
projects.summary: Campaign artwork for a volunteer beach cleanup.
body: A calm sea in four teals, with a pattern version for tote bags and volunteer shirts.
The artwork had to work printed in one colour as well as in full colour.

projects.title: Blue Notes gig posters
projects.summary: A season of posters for a small jazz club.
body: Sunflower yellow on deep indigo for every show, with the headline type changing size with the act.
The posters hang in a row outside the club, so they were designed to be read together.

projects.title: Crunch snack boxes
projects.summary: Bright boxes for a plant-based snack range.
body: Each flavour has its own colour, and the box shape is the same across the range to keep production simple.
The dieline uses one sheet and no glue.

projects.title: Forecast weather widget kit
projects.summary: A kit of weather widgets for phones and dashboards.
body: The kit covers small, medium and large widgets, each in light and dark.
Sky blue is the only accent; temperature is always the biggest number on screen.

projects.title: Bridges bilingual magazine
projects.summary: A redesign for a magazine printed in two languages side by side.
body: Both languages share every spread, with sapphire and cedar marking which is which.
The grid gives both columns the same measure, so neither language reads as the translation.

projects.title: Orbit rounded mono
projects.summary: A friendly rounded monospace for code and data.
body: Orbit softens every corner of a monospace without losing the clear zero, one and lowercase l.
The specimen shows it in a code editor and on a data table.

projects.title: Highline mountain lodge identity
projects.summary: A muted identity for a lodge above the tree line.
body: Sage and fir greys keep the identity quiet against the landscape.
The mark is engraved on room keys and printed on trail maps.
